criteria.evidence: No evidence of network effects or exponential value growth with scale
CSV processing and matching logic is stateless and horizontally scalable; adding more customers does not degrade performance for existing customers
SaaS delivery model is inherently more scalable than professional services alternatives
Digital delivery with no physical component means no fulfillment bottleneck

key_signals: No manual fulfillment or professional services component
SaaS model enables serving many customers simultaneously
analysis_narrative:
Scalability is a technical strength of this solution. The core matching algorithm — comparing transaction records by amount, date window, and customer ID — is a deterministic, stateless computation that is trivially parallelizable. A customer processing 10,000 transactions/month gets the same performance as one processing 100 transactions/month, with only cloud compute costs scaling proportionally.

The business model reinforces this: SaaS subscriptions create predictable revenue without proportional growth in support costs, assuming the product handles the common edge cases automatically. The founder's technical background is relevant here — they understand the matching problem deeply enough to build a robust solution.

Score 5 would require some form of value amplification with scale — network effects, data-driven matching improvements that compound with usage, or a platform that grows in value as more integrations are added. The current single-use-case positioning does not exhibit these properties.
key_finding: Scalability is technically sound — stateless CSV matching logic scales horizontally with no service degradation at volume.
score_explanation: Score 4 reflects a clean stateless architecture that scales with cloud infrastructure and a SaaS business model with high gross margins. Score 5 requires network effects or exponential value growth that are not present in the current solution design.
